1. Units and Measurement

Physics measures things with units. The SI (international) units are:

  • Length: metre (m)
  • Mass: kilogram (kg)
  • Time: second (s)
  • Force: newton (N)
  • Energy and work: joule (J)
  • Power: watt (W)

2. Scalars and Vectors

Scalar: has size only (distance, speed, mass, time).

Vector: has size and direction (displacement, velocity, force, momentum).

3. Motion

Speed = distance ÷ time

Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time

Free fall: acceleration due to gravity g = 9.8 m/s² (about 10 m/s²).

4. Newton's Laws

  • 1st law (inertia): an object stays at rest or keeps moving at constant velocity unless a force acts on it.
  • 2nd law: F = m × a
  • 3rd law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

5. Work, Energy and Power

Work = force × distance (in the direction of the force)

Kinetic energy = ½ × m × v²

Potential energy = m × g × h

Power = work ÷ time

Momentum = mass × velocity
